title: How to organize the workshop material rack
description:
Hold the wood and metal you will genuinely use, stored so it stays straight and does not fall on anyone.

This is The Material Rack in the Workshop. About 60-90 min.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE
Boards lying flat and supported along their length with the longest and heaviest at the bottom, sheet goods standing on edge against the wall rather than leaning out into the room, and an offcut bin with its size floor written on the front in marker. Nothing stored directly on the floor, and the route from the bench to the door clear along its full width.

THE SIX PASSES
Sort: Take the offcut bin apart piece by piece against a written size floor.
Straighten: Group by length and thickness so you can pull a board without unstacking three others, put pipe, trim, and dowel upright in a vertical bin, and support flat stock at intervals close enough that nothing sags between brackets.
Shine: Sweep out the gap behind the rack where sawdust, spider webs, and mouse droppings collect out of sight, then wipe surface rust off steel stock and give it a light oil before it goes back.
Safety: Fix the rack into structural framing, not just the wall skin, and load it heaviest at the bottom.
Standardize: Mark the lengths on the rack rails so stock returns to the right bay, write the size floor on the offcut bin, and mark a fill line above which the bin is full and the shortest piece leaves.
Sustain: Before you unplug the saw at the end of a cutting session, every offcut gets a verdict: the bin or the fire bucket.

THE STANDARD YOU LEAVE BEHIND
One offcut bin with a written size floor and a fill line, and nothing stored on the shop floor.

Full written steps for this zone, free:
